apps.name: Nova Launcher
apps.whats_new: AUTOMATIC GOLDFISH PICKUP. Build requests now send themselves: describe a feature in the Build door — by voice or typing — and it goes straight up to Nova on its own, no share sheet, no ferry step. Off the grid? The request waits on the phone and sends itself the moment you're back online. And Hear my builds tells the truth about every request: waiting to send (with the reason, in plain words), sent to Nova, or the drop-box's own words when a send doesn't go through. Requests the autopilot lane escalates ride the same pipe. The Share button stays as a spare key — pickup is automatic now.

apps.name: Nova Voice
apps.whats_new: Engine registration fix: Nova Voice now answers Android's engine-data checks (voice data check, sample text, install data) the way Google and Samsung's engines do — through 1.9 nothing answered those probes, and Nova never appeared in the Preferred engine lists. The app's top line now shows version 2.0 so you can confirm the update landed.

apps.name: Nova Phone
apps.whats_new: AGENT MODE. Nova now fronts your calls both ways. Incoming: she answers on speaker, says she is CodeStark's assistant, and handles the call by lane — friends and family get a casual hello and message-taking, businesses and unknown numbers get a professional intake (who, company, what about, is it urgent, best callback), and a caller you mark as heated gets listened to without an argument. Outgoing: give her a one-sentence errand and she makes the call herself — she never commits you to money, dates, or deals; anything bigger comes back to you as a question. After every agent call you get ONE summary: everything that matters, with the heat taken out. Lanes are set per person from Contacts or Recents; numbers you set to always ring through still ring to you; and you can grab any call back mid-sentence with the Take this call button. Honest limit, in plain words: Android gives regular apps no direct line into call audio, so Nova works through the speaker and the microphone, like someone sitting next to the phone — quiet rooms work best. Save your Gemini key in the Nova tab and she converses freely; without it she runs her scripted intake and the summary still lands. Agent Mode OFF means the phone works exactly like 1.6.

apps.name: Nova Chat
apps.whats_new: Fixes the blank screen — the app now actually shows the Watch List and Chat Reader.

apps.name: Nova Stream
apps.whats_new: Stream from the phone with RTMP — Twitch and YouTube starter buttons.

apps.name: UHC Claim Builder
apps.whats_new: Signature guaranteed: the form always prints your name as the signature with today's date beside it, the package-ready message reads the signature and date back to you before you send, and if your name is ever blank the package refuses to build instead of producing an unsigned form. New: a Send a test email button on the Build a Claim tab — it sends one clearly marked test email to UHC through your saved Gmail sign-in (no claim attached, no member ID) and, if it fails, shows the mail server's actual words so the problem names itself.

apps.name: Fanciful Companion
apps.whats_new: Fixed the 404 errors and long waits — she now finds the models your key can actually use and remembers the one that works, so answers come back fast.

apps.name: Nova House Log
apps.whats_new: House Sync is here — the old Nova trick at small scale. A tiny backend on Nova's side, reached through a tunnel, now serves Janelle's iPhone web app and syncs both ways with this app: her web entries fall into your Log tab automatically, labeled 'Janelle — via web app'; your entries and confirmation questions reach her side; and a question she answers with her OWN tap in the web app is stamped 'her own tap (web)' — stronger than a verbal answer recorded by you. New Sync tab: server address is pre-filled (editable — tunnel addresses change; Nova can read you the current one) and you paste the app key Nova gives you once. Sync runs when the app opens and on Sync Now, and speaks what arrived ('Synced: 2 new entries from Janelle'). Failures speak honestly and never touch your local log.

apps.name: Nova Devotion
apps.whats_new: First release: a daily devotion on your phone — today's verse and reflection spoken in Nova's voice, all 14 banked devotions by ear, and a morning reminder if you want one.

apps.name: Pastor Nova
apps.whats_new: Two fixes from the field: (1) Sermon generation no longer dies when one Google model has a network hiccup — she walks to the next model — and if a fresh sermon still can't be generated, the fallback now speaks Google's actual reason out loud instead of just naming a code. (2) Worship: songs are now picked preferring the uploads YouTube actually allows embedded players to play (Topic-channel and official-audio posts over label music videos), and if three songs in a row still fail, she stops, says why once, and moves on with the service instead of silently skipping through the whole list.

apps.name: Nova Music
apps.whats_new: Nova Music is here. Search any song and play it, build your own playlists and play them straight through, say a song name out loud to search by voice, and use Name That Song — type some lyrics or describe the song and Nova figures out what it is, then finds it for you. It borrows your Gemini key from the Launcher automatically, so there's nothing to set up.

apps.name: Nova Bible
apps.whats_new: New in 1.1: the New Living Translation (NLT) is here. Tap the translation button on the book list to cycle to NLT — it works everywhere KJV does: chapter reading, read-aloud, chapter and verse commentary, and the Find tab, with the text fetched fresh for you.

apps.name: Nova RD
apps.whats_new: New in 1.8: (1) Guard Mode now hands its incidents to Nova House Log. When Guard trips, House Log gets a draft incident built only from what Guard measures — the time, how long the sound lasted, how loud it got. Never words, never who was talking: Guard hears loudness, not speech. The draft waits in House Log for your confirmation and never counts on its own, and a copy stays in RD's Log either way, marked sent or not sent with the plain reason. There's a switch for it on the Guard tab, on by default. (2) The message cleanup tells the truth now. Cody's 1.7 test caught it handing his words straight back and calling them cleaned. Now the result is compared against what you wrote: if the model just echoes you, RD retries once with a blunt rewrite-only instruction, and if it still comes back unchanged it says so plainly — it will not call an untouched message cleaned. Everything else — the gate, Guard Mode, Amen's standing rules and contingencies — works exactly as before.
